title: Program Kit integration and release provenance
intent: Make repository CI, rather than individual development sessions, prove combined changes; build one publication-eligible package set from trusted main; and publish only those exact prebuilt bytes after explicit human dispatch.
scope: One stable integration check for pull_request and merge_group combined-source validation.
One trusted main-push canonical package build using the existing finite release-package manifest and aggregate consumer-feed packer.
Exact build provenance binding source commit, workflow run, workflow definition, integration profile, package inventory, package bytes, checksums, and artifact identity.
A human-dispatched protected publication workflow that retrieves one exact eligible main-build artifact, verifies it, and publishes without rebuilding.
A provider-neutral contributor lifecycle in which local agents perform focused work and use CI status as shared integration evidence.
A planning-contract evolution that separates human-approved semantic obligations from compatible execution-resolved verification evidence.
Repository documentation and a finite human-owned GitHub settings handoff for rulesets, merge queue, protected environment, and trusted publishing.
nonGoals: Automatically approving, merging, releasing, publishing, retrying, or changing repository settings.
Eliminating local focused tests, real source-conflict resolution, human review, or material compatibility decisions.
Publishing pull-request or merge-group artifacts, executing untrusted artifact code with elevated permissions, or using pull_request_target.
Creating a new C# analyzer, extending the private Program Kit gate, or attaching it to consumer-owned source.
Changing the finite first-party package inventory, package version, package contents, NuGet identity, or dependency topology merely to establish CI.
Making coordinated multi-package publication atomic when the external registry provides no transaction.
Adding provider-specific agent behavior, hooks, watchers, plugins, autonomous loops, or user-global configuration.
Mutating the parent Domain Semantic Engine repository or any other consumer repository.
assumptions: The repository remains hosted on GitHub and its default protected integration branch is main.
The existing canonical release-package manifest and Invoke-PackConsumerFeed.ps1 remain the source of package inventory and exact package/checksum generation.
The existing NuGet trusted-publishing relationship can be updated or confirmed by the human without introducing a long-lived package-feed API key.
The repository owner can configure a required check, merge queue, and protected publication environment after the workflow files merge.
The existing private Program Kit C# gate remains compatible with applicable Program Kit-owned implementation source.
GitHub-hosted artifacts and attestations remain available under the repository plan and retention settings.

sourceTruthAuthorities.governs: The human outcome, approval-versus-execution boundary, publication authority, development-session efficiency, and administrative handoff.
The implemented workflow that currently rebuilds and publishes in one privileged job and therefore defines the replacement boundary.
The finite manifest-selected restore, build, no-build/no-restore pack, package inspection, SHA-256 package manifest, and checksum output.
The reviewed GitHub pull-request, merge-group, merge-queue, artifact, attestation, ruleset, and environment behavior used by this design.

domains.purpose: Own combined-source verification, build-run eligibility, approval-versus-execution bindings, and CI evidence without taking human authority.

vocabulary.meaning: The exact synthetic pull-request merge commit or merge-group commit evaluated by the required integration workflow.
A successful trusted push run for main that passes integration and produces one exact package artifact eligible for later publication.
A semantically constrained verification selection whose exact revision and digest are resolved and recorded at execution time rather than embedded as immutable human-approved product semantics.

domains.purpose: Own exact package inventory, package-byte evidence, checksum closure, artifact retrieval, and no-rebuild publication.

vocabulary.meaning: The complete finite package feed, package manifest, checksums, and CI provenance emitted by one eligible canonical build.
Publication that verifies and transmits the selected canonical package set without restore, compile, test, generation, or pack.

semanticModels.meaning: Separates semantic obligations requiring exact human approval from compatible verification revisions whose exact bytes become run evidence.
semanticModels.invariants: Every binding declares its resolution mode. Approval-fixed references retain identity, version, and digest. Execution-resolved references retain an approved identity and compatibility policy while the exact selected version and digest are recorded by the trusted run. A semantic, authority, or compatibility-policy change is never treated as mechanical drift.

semanticModels.meaning: The closed evidence that makes one main build and its package set eligible for human-dispatched publication.
semanticModels.invariants: Repository, branch, event, source commit, workflow identity, workflow revision, run ID, verification profile, release-package manifest digest, package manifest digest, checksum digest, package identities, sizes, and SHA-256 digests are complete and mutually consistent.

components.purpose: Run one stable read-only integration check for pull-request and merge-group combined source and the same integration profile before canonical main packaging.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Trigger events, stable job name, checkout semantics, read-only permissions, cancellation policy, integration entrypoint, and required observations.

components.purpose: After successful integration on a trusted main push, create, verify, attest, and upload one complete canonical package set.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Push-to-main eligibility, finite package selection, packer invocation, provenance fields, checksums, attestation subjects, immutable artifact identity, and retention.

components.purpose: Retrieve one human-selected eligible main build, verify exact provenance and package bytes, obtain temporary credentials through a protected environment, publish, and create durable release assets.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Manual input, protected branch and environment, run metadata, artifact identity, checksums, no-rebuild rule, temporary credential timing, package push, tag target, and release assets.

components.purpose: Validate approval-fixed and execution-resolved plan bindings and reject semantic drift disguised as a mechanical digest refresh.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Planning schema revision, resolution modes, compatible selection rules, exact execution receipt, and material-change diagnostics.

referenceRules.referencingScope: The required integration workflow for pull_request and merge_group
referenceRules.referencedScope: The event-provided synthetic combined commit and repository-owned integration profile at that commit
referenceRules.rationale: GitHub owns synthesis of current combined source; CI proves it once for all contributors without requiring every branch to reproduce the merge locally.

referenceRules.referencedScope: Exactly one successful canonical package artifact from a push run of the registered integration workflow on main
referenceRules.rationale: The publication job must consume trusted prebuilt bytes and must not accept same-named artifacts from pull requests, merge groups, arbitrary branches, failed runs, or another workflow.

referenceRules.referencedScope: A synthesized merge SHA, hosted run ID, artifact ID, or compatible current verification-profile digest as if it were immutable product intent
referenceRules.rationale: Execution evidence must be exact, but compatible execution facts are resolved after approval and must not force renewed semantic approval.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the exact combined-source integration, approval-versus-execution, canonical package-build, and no-rebuild publication design as one canonical review artifact.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design records architecture and grants no workflow execution, settings mutation, package publication, or implementation authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The design is schema-validated, rendered for review, and bound by an exact implementation plan and review manifest.

agentRetrieval.rationale: No runtime agent retrieval, provider integration, or capability delivery is created.

agentProcedure.rationale: Workflow automation begins only on explicit repository events configured and authorized by humans.

humanCommunication.audience: The Program Kit repository owner, reviewers, implementation contributors, and release operator.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of the exact canonical design and plan digests authorizes implementation; publication and external settings remain separate human actions.
humanCommunication.rationale: The change redistributes integration work and creates a privileged package-publication boundary.

generatedNavigation.rationale: No repository-wide generated index is required.

governance.provenancePolicy: The human intent, exact source commit, repository source files, platform evidence, and static decision are named; future workflow runs do not retroactively become design authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest binds exact canonical design and plan bytes. Any material change requires revalidation, new digests, and a new human decision.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Changing integration events, required outcomes, trust boundary, package eligibility, publication authority, no-rebuild rule, or approval-versus-execution semantics requires a reviewed design revision.
governance.migrationPolicy: The implementation introduces new planning and provenance revisions beside existing readable artifacts and updates active capability guidance without rewriting historical approvals.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: The design contains no credentials, tokens, package-feed secrets, consumer data, or user-local paths.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Only committed review artifacts, public documentation references, exact digests, and non-secret workflow evidence may be shared.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Run IDs, synthetic commits, artifact IDs, temporary credentials, package staging, and local build output remain execution evidence outside the canonical design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A canonical design is required because this change alters planning admissibility, shared integration ownership, supply-chain provenance, and release authority rather than merely editing one workflow.

security.policy: Untrusted combined-source checks are read-only and secretless; elevated publication never executes pull-request code or accepts an unverified artifact.
guarantees: Pull-request and merge-group jobs use least privileges and no publication environment.
Canonical build eligibility requires a successful push event for main.
Publication verifies run metadata and artifact bytes before credentials are requested.
exclusions: Self-hosted runners, pull_request_target builds, arbitrary workflow_run promotion, and long-lived package-feed keys are not introduced.

authority.policy: Humans approve semantics, merge changes, configure repository protections, dispatch publication, approve the protected environment, and own material recovery.
guarantees: CI reports evidence but does not approve or merge.
A successful canonical build does not publish automatically.
Compatible execution resolution cannot widen approved scope or authority.
exclusions: No recommendation, status check, artifact, attestation, or agent action originates human authority.

secrets.policy: Only the protected publication job requests a temporary NuGet credential after exact artifact verification.
guarantees: Integration and canonical-build jobs need no package-feed secret.
Environment secrets remain unavailable until protection rules pass.
exclusions: Credentials are never uploaded, attested, logged, embedded in packages, or exposed to untrusted source.

persistence.policy: Repository source owns workflows and verification rules; one workflow-run artifact owns transient canonical bytes; a completed GitHub release preserves durable public release assets.
guarantees: Package manifest and SHA256SUMS enumerate every canonical package.
The publisher does not mutate or replace selected package bytes.
exclusions: Caches, obj/bin output, agent worktrees, and pull-request artifacts are not publication authority.

failure.policy: Missing checks, failed tests, stale or incompatible execution selections, ineligible run metadata, missing or extra packages, digest mismatch, absent attestation, or authority denial fails closed.
guarantees: No canonical artifact is uploaded after failed integration.
No package is pushed before the complete selected artifact verifies.
Material plan drift returns to human design review.
exclusions: A partial external NuGet publication cannot be rolled back automatically and requires explicit human recovery.

concurrency.policy: Superseded pull-request runs may be cancelled; merge-group and publication runs are never cancelled by a newer unrelated event; one publication per package version is serialized.
guarantees: Merge-queue evidence always corresponds to the active merge group.
Two publication runs cannot race the same coordinated package version.
exclusions: No development session repeatedly synchronizes main solely to emulate queue serialization.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation before publication leaves repository and registry unchanged; cancellation during external package pushes reports partial state and stops before tag or release creation.
guarantees: Temporary build and download roots are non-authoritative.
No automatic retry or alternate artifact selection occurs.
exclusions: The workflow does not claim atomic compensation for external package pushes.

observability.policy: Stable checks and provenance expose event, exact commit, workflow/run identity, profile selection, package inventory, checksums, artifact identity, publication input, and final release target without secrets.
guarantees: Agents and humans can wait on one shared integration result instead of reproducing it locally.
Every published package maps to one exact canonical build and source commit.
exclusions: Logs do not become approval records and telemetry beyond GitHub/NuGet workflow evidence is not introduced.

compatibility.policy: Semantic approval bindings remain exact; execution-resolved bindings accept only explicitly compatible profile revisions and record the exact selected bytes.
guarantees: A material integration or publication change requires renewed design approval.
A compatible current verification implementation can produce new execution evidence without rewriting approved product semantics.
Historical plan, disposition, and execution receipts remain immutable.
exclusions: Matching names, branches, artifact labels, or versions alone never establish eligibility or compatibility.

scenarios.intent: Prove one proposed change against current main without repeatedly merging main into the contributor branch.
preconditions: A pull request targets main and the workflow file exists on the default branch.
steps: GitHub synthesizes and checks out the pull-request merge commit.
The read-only integration job runs the repository-owned verification profile and reports one stable check.
If main changes while the pull request remains mergeable, GitHub synthesizes current combined source and reruns the check.
The contributor responds to real conflicts or failing evidence rather than mechanically reproducing CI.
outcomes: Reviewers share one exact combined-source result.
No publication artifact or credential is created.
failureOutcomes: A conflict, failing test, missing check, or incompatible profile blocks queue entry or merge.

scenarios.intent: Prove multiple accepted changes together on the latest target branch before merge.
preconditions: The repository ruleset requires merge queue and the stable integration check.
steps: The operator adds an approved pull request to the queue.
GitHub constructs a merge group from current main and queued changes.
The same required integration job runs for merge_group checks_requested.
GitHub merges only the successful current group.
outcomes: Cross-agent compatibility is proven once at the integration authority.
Behind branches need no strict pre-queue main merge when still mergeable.
failureOutcomes: A failed or missing group check removes or blocks the affected queue entry.

scenarios.intent: Create one exact publication-eligible package set from a trusted merged main commit.
preconditions: A push event targets main and integration succeeds for its exact commit.
steps: Run the exhaustive repository integration profile.
Invoke the existing finite consumer-feed packer once.
Write CI provenance for the exact commit, workflow, run, profile, source manifest, package manifest, and checksums.
Verify the complete package set, attest package subjects, and upload one immutable named artifact.
outcomes: The artifact is eligible for later human selection.
Every package byte has exact local and hosted provenance evidence.
failureOutcomes: Any integration, pack, inventory, checksum, provenance, attestation, or upload failure leaves no eligible canonical build.

scenarios.intent: Publish one selected canonical main build without rebuilding it.
preconditions: The operator supplies one exact successful canonical-build run ID and passes the protected publication environment.
steps: Verify the selected run is completed successfully, came from the registered workflow, event push, branch main, and a commit in protected main history.
Download exactly the expected artifact and verify its hosted identity plus internal provenance, package manifest, SHA256SUMS, package count, names, sizes, and digests.
Request the temporary NuGet credential only after verification.
Push the exact package files without restore, build, test, generation, or pack.
Create the matching tag and release at the canonical-build commit and attach the exact packages, manifest, checksums, and provenance.
outcomes: Published packages trace to one exact merged commit and canonical build.
Durable GitHub release assets preserve the selected evidence after workflow-artifact expiry.
failureOutcomes: Ineligible metadata, digest drift, missing package, environment denial, credential failure, registry failure, or release mismatch fails closed and reports any partial external publication.

statusClaims.claim: The repository already has a manifest-driven aggregate packer that emits an exact package manifest and SHA256SUMS.
The current workflow rebuilds, tests, packs, authenticates, publishes, tags, and releases in one job; it is source truth to replace, not acceptance evidence for the proposed separation.
No pull-request or merge-group integration workflow is implemented yet.
No verified no-rebuild publisher or protected publication environment binding is implemented yet.
